editorial: Don’t Look Up flips the newsroom into a carnival of soundbites, luring you through dazzling media spectacle that feels like a feverish news anchor tour. Its satire builds on your discomfort with an escalating absurdity, making every headline feel like a quick-witted jab at real-time politics. Joaquin Phoenix and Leonardo DiCaprio command the spectacle with near-asynchronous performances that slice through the noise, yet the third act’s falter leaves your adrenaline flagging. You’ll appreciate the film’s razor-sharp social commentary, but pacing glitches might leave you a tad impatient. The film demands an audience keen on clever, politically annihilated humor and a refusal to take the status quo lightly.
targetAudience: Ideal for viewers who enjoy biting political satire that blurs the line between humor and sobering commentary.
